Want to rent a dog for the day? Borrow a shelter dog instead

⁠​‍⁢‍‌‌​⁢⁢‍‌‍​‍‌⁢⁠Dog rental businesses are rare and controversial, but hundreds of animal shelters let you borrow a dog for free. You get a hiking buddy or a couch companion for the day; the dog gets a break from the kennel and a better shot at adoption. Shelters call it Doggy Day Out, Dog for a Day, Foster a Dog for a Day, Field Trips, Daycations, Rent-A-Dog or Borrow a Buddy. A few shelters even let you take out puppies.

Good to know

Is borrowing a shelter dog free?

Yes, almost always. Shelters provide a leash, an Adopt Me vest and often treats and a water bowl.

What do I need to borrow a dog?

Usually a photo ID, being 18 or older, and a signed waiver. Some shelters need a short orientation or an online booking first.

How long can I keep the dog?

Day trips run from a couple of hours to a full day. Many shelters also offer overnights, weekend sleepovers or week-long staycations.

ShelterDayOut is a free directory. We don't run outings or handle bookings; each shelter sets its own rules. Listings are checked monthly, but details change, so confirm with the shelter before you go.

Ready to adopt? ShelterAdoption, our sister site, lists every shelter near you plus upcoming adoption events.
